web_evidence.title: Dead in the Family — publisher-formatted excerpt
web_evidence.note: A sustained seven-page opening excerpt repeatedly presents Sookie's actions, memories, perceptions, and private thoughts as “I,” establishing first-person narration for the opening.

web_evidence.title: Between the Lines with Charlaine Harris
web_evidence.note: In this author interview, Harris describes the Sookie books collectively as years of first-person feminine writing and says she kept the books anchored on Sookie.

web_evidence.title: The Southern Vampire Mysteries
web_evidence.note: The series overview explicitly says the series is narrated in first person by Sookie Stackhouse and identifies Dead in the Family as its tenth novel.

person_note: The diagnostic quotes repeatedly expose Sookie as a participating “I” narrator across actions, perceptions, and private reflection. Dialogue-only pronouns and Eric's embedded note were not allowed to vote as base narration, although narratorial framing around several dialogue passages independently confirms first person. The sustained opening excerpt agrees, and whole-series descriptions—including Harris's own account—identify the Sookie novels as first-person writing anchored on Sookie. No credible evidence of sustained second- or third-person sections was found; the only scope limitation is that the authorized prose source covers the opening rather than the complete novel.
